PullRequest.Title: sessions: fix compact view state transitions
PullRequest.Body:
Follow-up to #336169 addressing the two Copilot Code Review findings that landed after auto-merge.

- keeps compact workspace metadata hidden for pinned rows at rest and after DOM focus leaves the list
- rerenders compact presentation and row heights across desktop/phone layout transitions
- adds focused coverage for pinned/stale focus and desktop → phone → desktop transitions

Validation:
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- ESLint and stylelint for changed files
- full Sessions list suite: 112 passing

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The added line, synchronous call path, all-history loops, allocations, replacing tree splice, and viewport breakpoint trigger are directly established in repository code. Exact list sizes and milliseconds vary by user, so severity is medium, but the broadened mechanism is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work, temporary tree/chat objects, observable subscriptions, and visible-row DOM
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each desktop/phone breakpoint crossing now filters and groups all known sessions, sorts group/section members, creates a SessionChatItem and tree description for every included chat, and replaces the tree model; cost grows with total included session/chat history rather than only the rows whose presentation is onscreen.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased synchronous resize/orientation latency, CPU/GC pressure, and potential dropped frames
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The handler walked the existing tree and called updateElementHeight for session/chat nodes, avoiding session regrouping/sorting, new chat/tree object allocation, and row-template rebinding.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The handler calls setCompact(), which toggles the class and synchronously calls update(); update rebuilds the entire hierarchy and passes it to tree.setChildren before the context-key notification returns.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 3041 replaces the prior existing-tree height reconciliation with this.setCompact(); setCompact synchronously invokes the full update() path.
Findings.Title: Avoid rebuilding the sessions tree on breakpoint changes
Findings.Impact: Dragging a Sessions window across the phone breakpoint, or rotating a device with a large session/chat history, can synchronously rebuild the whole list on each threshold crossing and make the layout transition stutter; repeatedly oscillating around the breakpoint repeats the work.
Findings.Evidence: The added call reaches SessionsList.setCompact (lines 3712-3714), which calls update(). update() filters all sessions, sorts grouped/section sessions, maps every included session and chat into new tree elements (including new SessionChatItem objects), then invokes tree.setChildren(null, children) and recreates chat-height tracking. The ObjectTree identity provider is not passed as a diffIdentityProvider to this setChildren call, so ObjectTreeModel uses a replacing splice; visible renderer templates clear and recreate reactive subscriptions and details DOM. The phone context is synchronously driven by viewportClass, placing this work directly on the resize/orientation transition path.
Findings.Recommendation: Use a dedicated presentation refresh for breakpoint changes: toggle the compact class, rerender affected visible rows, and reconcile row heights in a batched tree/list operation without regrouping, sorting, or replacing the sessions model.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or rotate the Sessions workbench across the desktop/phone breakpoint while the sessions list is populated
Scenarios.CriticalPath: viewportClass updates IsPhoneLayoutContext synchronously; the changed context listener calls setCompact(), which cannot return until update() has filtered, grouped, sorted, allocated the replacement hierarchy, called tree.setChildren, reconciled chat approvals, and notified update listeners. This work is directly on the layout-transition critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total included non-automation session history plus every included session's visible-model chat count; date grouping and expanded/uncapped workspace groups can retain far more model rows than fit in the viewport, while DOM rendering is virtualized to visible rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The context-key listener is synchronous and uncoalesced. One rebuild runs per actual breakpoint crossing; repeated threshold crossings during window dragging serialize as repeated full rebuilds.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cached presentation tree or coalescing prevents repeated update() work across crossings. Renderer virtualization bounds simultaneous DOM rows but not all-session filtering/grouping/sorting/tree allocation. Automations badge initialization is guarded by initializationPromise, so it does not repeat its asynchronous assignment lookup on this path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line synchronously reaches the complete update() implementation, and the replacement tree construction and all-history loops are explicit. The old handler performed existing-node height reconciliation without model regrouping/sorting/reallocation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The precise history size and duration vary, and a typical default-filtered list may be small; users with large active histories, many chats, expanded groups, or repeated resize crossings see the strongest effect.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium rendering regression: the diff materially broadens breakpoint work from height reconciliation to a full model and visible-row presentation rebuild, creating avoidable CPU/GC and transition-jank risk.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover and keyboard-focus transitions for compact session rows, including pinned rows and focus leaving the list
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The browser updates :hover/:focus-within matching and row presentation styles during pointer/focus processing. No JavaScript, model refresh, or external operation was added to this path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: CSS matching is scoped to the sessions list and its currently focused or hovered row; list virtualization bounds live row DOM.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser style recalculation is synchronous with each pointer/focus transition; there is no application queue or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Browser style-system caching applies normally; the diff adds no application cache or retained state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the selector change only narrows when compact metadata is displayed; no evidence establishes added scaling work or retention.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser selector invalidation cost is implementation-dependent, but the selector is scoped and the live DOM is virtualized.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the CSS change removes the pinned-row match and scopes focused-row styling under list focus, without introducing a concrete expensive mechanism.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all three changed files and traced breakpoint and focus/hover scenarios. Submitted one medium-confidence-high finding for synchronous full-tree reconstruction on each phone/desktop breakpoint crossing; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network fan-out was introduced, and the CSS/test changes add no production performance issue.
